# 8086-emu — hook spec (for emulator agent)

Package: `8086emu` first-party source (`/home/danish1075/Documents/8086`, branch
`main` + uncommitted 1.6-staged circuit-board hooks on top of the `1.5.1`
release). Our runner: `OpenHW-studio-frontend/src/worker/runners/retro-runner.ts`.
Our vendor bytes: `public/vendor/board-engines/8086emu/` (glue
`multi_cpu_emu.js` + `multi_cpu_emu_bg.wasm`) and the live copy the runner
actually fetches, `public/wasm/multi_cpu_emu_bg.wasm` (runner:
`retro-runner.ts:195-206`, `fetch` + `initSync({ module })` — the pattern the
package's own `8086api.md §2` documents for Node).

Status (2026-10-06): the runner-side wiring for the 1.6 hooks is DONE and
additive-only (feature-detected with `typeof` guards, old engine bytes still
work). Engine side is staged-unreleased in `/home/danish1075/Documents/8086`
(`CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased]`); every claim below is verified against
`8086api.md` + `CHANGELOG.md` + `docs/pkg/multi_cpu_emu.d.ts` in that tree.

## Landed hooks (engine 1.6-staged — what our runner now relies on)

1. **PPI input latch** — `ppi_set_input(port, v)` (`multi_cpu_emu.d.ts:170`,
   `CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased]`): drives the 8255 external-input latch for
   8086/8085, `port` is `0xE0` (A) / `0xE1` (B) / `0xE2` (C). Input-mode bits
   read back the injected pins; output-mode bits keep the firmware latch;
   snapshot/restore covers the latch. Our runner (`retro-runner.ts:326-333`)
   RMWs one bit through it and keeps the old output-latch RMW
   (`retro-runner.ts:334-350`) as fallback when `ppi_set_input` is absent.
2. **Universal serial RX** — `usart_rx(v)` + `usart_status()`
   (`multi_cpu_emu.d.ts:292-299`, `CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased]`): routed per
   ISA — 8086/8085/Z80 kit USART (ports `0x50`/`0x51`), 6502 board ACIA
   (`$5000`/`$5001`), 8051 SBUF/SCON (status bit1 = RI, bit2 = TI), rv32
   board UART (`0xF0000`). Our runner (`retro-runner.ts:261`) routes ALL ISAs
   through it first; legacy aliases (`push_key`, `serial_rx`, `set_sid`) are
   the fallback only. Older per-ISA names keep working (engine guarantee).
3. **Cycle clock on all ISAs** — `cycles()->bigint`
   (`multi_cpu_emu.d.ts:39`): machine cycles/T-states for 8086/8085/8051,
   nominal per-instruction tables for 6502/Z80, single-cycle for rv32; covered
   by snapshot/restore. Our runner (`retro-runner.ts:222-247`) returns the
   per-tick cycle delta as the `stepBudget` result so base `simCycleCount`
   advances in engine cycles; falls back to the executed-step count when
   `cycles` is absent (previous behavior, bit-identical).
4. **rv32 board GPIO** — `port_write(0xE0, v)` injects GPIO pins,
   `port_read(0xE0/0xE1)` reads DATA/DIR (`multi_cpu_emu.d.ts:155-159`,
   engine `AGENTS.md` rv32 section). Single DATA byte: our runner
   (`retro-runner.ts:286-299`) merges both pin groups onto `0xE0`. On old
   engine bytes `port_write` is a no-op, so the call stays inert there.
5. **USART Tx cap** — the 8251 Tx queue is capped at 1024 bytes, oldest
   dropped (`CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased]` — same rationale as the
   program-output cap). Matches our runner-side 4096 TX-queue cap; no runner
   change needed.
6. **Snapshot forward-tolerance** — old snapshots stay loadable: the 8085
   i8155/cycle-clock offset fix keeps the old layout readable, and
   `Via6522::restore` accepts the exact 20-byte form (`CHANGELOG.md
   [Unreleased]`). Runner implication: step-back/record-replay across a
   vendor refresh must not be treated as corrupt — surface a clean error,
   never garbage state.

## What to expose (stable JS ABI — freeze these)

`ppi_set_input`, `usart_rx`, `usart_status`, `cycles`, plus the existing
`port_read`/`port_write`, `push_key`, `serial_rx`, `set_sid`, `snapshot` /
`restore`, `reset`, `via_pins`, `mem_size` — all already used by our runner
or the board views; keep signatures frozen. (`via_pins`, `i2c_dump`,
`rtc_write`, `mem_size` board helpers from 1.5.1 are available but unwired —
P1 candidates, see below.)

## Constraints

- Additive-only; when the new calls are absent the runner behaves exactly as
  on 1.5.1 bytes (RMW paths, step-count sim-time, inert rv32 input).
- No firmware-specific casing: the USART/ACIA/board-UART paths must behave
  identically for hand-assembled and IDE-assembled guests (same ports, same
  queues).

## Cross-cutting constraints (sync/SAB — engine side of the contract)

Engines never touch SharedArrayBuffer: each engine runs as a plain
synchronous step function inside its board Worker, and only our
`arm-runner-base.ts` touches SAB (pin bitfields, barrier cells, STEP
collect). Two things the engine must still guarantee so multi-board
lockstep holds:

1. **Reset clears everything, synchronously** — cores, peripherals, pending
   events, USART/Rx queues, cycle clock, and any `stopped`/fault flags. A
   sticky flag desyncs one board's lane forever while the others advance.
   (Engine reports this for the 1.6 reset path; the wasm `reset()` doc-comment
   still says "memory preserved" — stale. The contract here wins: reset must
   leave no observable pre-reset state except loaded memory/ROM images.)
2. **Expose a cycle/instruction counter per step** — landed as `cycles()` on
   all six ISAs (§3 above); feeds sim-time edge stamps (replacing the
   runner's step-count approximation) and the skew/pace accounting. One
   counter serves both.

## Further surface (same agent — already present, runner-unwired P1)

7. **ADC/LCD/RTC/DMA kit readback** (`adc_get`, `lcd_text`, `rtc_reg`,
   `dma_status`, `kb_disp`) — wire to sensor/display/dial components.
8. **Interrupt injection** (`interrupt(kind, data)` per-ISA kinds,
   `set_interrupt_mode`, `ctc_pulse`) — fault/test injection + timer IRQ cells.
9. **Memory/ROM windows** (`mem_size`, `rom_region`/`set_rom_region`,
   `sram_region`, `flash_region`, `fs_put`/`fs_get`) — memory-map + file
   injection UI without per-ISA hardcoding.
10. **Debug stepping** (`run_bp`/`run_to`, `waiting_input`, `disasm`,
    `assemble_info`, `set_reg`) — PC breakpoints at chunk boundary (note:
    `run_to`/`run_bp` targets are NOT executed — the runner must account the
    off-by-one).

## Future-component guarantee (signal-level contract)

Components are unbounded — so the promise is per **primitive**, not per part.
After §1–6, ANY future component built on these works with zero further
engine changes (only generic runner-bridge mapping):

- GPIO out edge + level, GPIO in inject (direction-merged, never clobbers
  firmware outputs), UART both directions + status bits, per-step
  cycle/instruction counters for sim-time stamps.
- P2 engine ask (not blocking): PIT/CTC/VIA-timer tick readback for
  timer/PWM components (`pit_count`, `ctc_count` exist; VIA T1 readback does
  not yet).

## Known limits (engine-documented, runner must respect)

- 6502 cycles are nominal (base costs, branches-taken, NO page-cross penalty;
  +7 per interrupt entry) and Z80 cycles are table-nominal (+11 NMI / +13 INT
  acknowledge) — host sim-time only, not logic-analyzer grade.
- rv32 `cycles()` is +1 per retired step; rv32 has NO interrupt model
  (`interrupt()` throws) and no CLINT/PLIC.
- 6502 ACIA lives at `$5000`–`$5003`: keep firmware code AND data clear of
  the block (debugger `mem()`/disasm peek without consuming, but `LDA $5000`
  pops Rx).
- rv32 board block at `0xF0000` is byte `LB`/`SB` access only.
- Z80 `port_read(0x50)` stays a plain latch (never consumes Rx); `IN A,(50h)`
  pops the host-injected queue — the two paths are deliberately split,
  mirroring 8086/8085.
- 8051 `usart_status` is mapped from SCON, not a real 8251 register.
- `out()` drain: 8086 INT 21h AH=09 leaves NUL padding + trailing code bytes
  (runner strips `\0`; `retro-runner.ts:236-240`).

## Acceptance (our e2e, already written)

- `tests/e2e/retro-boards.spec.js`: 8086/8085/8051/6502/Z80 console needles
  (`HELLO_R86`, `HELLO_R85`, `HELLO_R51`, `Hi`, `Hi`) via in-WASM
  `assemble()` — must stay green across the vendor refresh.
- `tests/e2e/retro-gpio.spec.js`: LED lights via GPIO (8086/8085/6502/Z80
  full light; 8051 quasi-bidirectional LOW-drive) — must stay green; proves
  `ppi_set_input` / VIA / latch paths output-side.
